prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1440; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: The claim was opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection, and the claimant's attorney has since notified us of representation. Initial contact with the claimant has been routed through counsel.

Entry 2: The driver of the insured vehicle is a resident of the policyholder's household and is listed as a covered household member under the policy. Coverage eligibility has been confirmed for this loss.

Entry 3: Scene photographs were received and show the rear bumper, tail lamp assembly, and trunk lid damage consistent with the reported impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main visual record of the event.

Entry 4: The police report and statements from the parties confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision. No earlier damage to the claimant's vehicle has come to light in our review of prior claims and inspection records.

Entry 5: Medical records show a diagnosis of a neck strain, which fits the type and force of a rear-end impact of this kind. No prior injury to the neck or upper back has been identified in the claimant's records.

Entry 6: Treatment has followed a typical course, with therapy visits tapering as the claimant's range of motion improved. It is not yet clear whether all of the vehicle damage in the repair estimate resulted from this impact, so the supplement is under review.

Entry 7: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation, including through counsel. Nothing in the file suggests that the damage occurred before the coverage period began.

Entry 8: Next steps are to request the remaining treatment billing through counsel and to complete the damage review with the repair shop before the valuation is finalized.
